name: אֲחִירָם
summary: A son of Benjamin, head of the family of the Ahiramites in the second census (Num 26:38); TIPNR takes him to be the Ehi of Gen 46:21 and the Aharah of 1Ch 8:1. The name is אָחִי “my brother” with רָם “high, exalted”: “my brother is exalted”, the brother being a kinsman or God, as in the parallel names אֲבִירָם and אֲדֹנִירָם. The same name, ʾḥrm, was borne by a king of Byblos whose sarcophagus is inscribed in Phoenician.

evidence.note: “The sons of Benjamin by their families … of אֲחִירָם, the family of the Ahiramites.”
“Benjamin fathered Bela his firstborn, Ashbel the second, and Aharah the third.”
“וְרָם הוּא above all the peoples”: the second element.

note: BDB's a.ck.ax has one token (Num 26:38). The ach entry's note leaves the names in אֲחִי- to be filed under their second element. TIPNR's identification of Ahiram with Ehi and Aharah rests on the order of the lists, not on any statement of scripture; the keys for אֵחִי and אַחְרַח (a.cp.aj) are not claimed here. The Phoenician Ahiram of Byblos is noted under the ach entry (KAI 1); his inscription was not cited for this name.
